name: Supermicro

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Super Micro Computer Logo.svg)

description: Supermicro designs and assembles servers and storage systems, mostly GPU-based AI servers (increasingly sold as complete liquid- or air-cooled racks under its Data Center Building Block Solutions), plus subsystems and accessories and support services. It makes money on the system sale itself, at thin hardware margins (gross margin about 10.8% in FY2026), so profit depends on enormous volume: net sales rose 78% to $39.1B in FY2026 and operating income to $2.77B (7.1%). One customer was 28.1% of FY2026 sales and 71% of sales were to the U.S. Services and software, the recurring part, were only $538M (1.4%). It carries heavy legal and regulatory overhang: SEC and Justice Department inquiries, securities class actions and an export-control indictment of three people tied to the company.

sub.name: Data-center networking, servers, optics and cooling

gics.note: Conventional GICS sector and sub-industry as listed in Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies), read 2026-10-01; industry group and industry are not shown there. SEC SIC 3571 (Electronic Computers).

hq.note: 980 Rock Avenue, San Jose, CA (10-K cover)

employees.note: over 7,000: about 3,500 R&D, 800 sales and marketing, 600 G&A, 2,100 manufacturing

businessLines.name: Server and storage systems, subsystems and accessories, and services (single business)
businessLines.how: One-time hardware sale per server or rack (built from in-house modular building blocks around third-party GPUs and CPUs), plus on-site support service plans; services and software were $538.3M of FY2026 sales.
businessLines.description: AI, cloud, enterprise and edge servers and storage (rackmount, blade, multi-node), complete rack-scale systems, plus server boards, chassis, power supplies and Global Services support plans. The split between systems and subsystems was not captured.
